Correct Inter-Detector Elution Delays

Source: R/step_sec_detector_delay.R
step_sec_detector_delay.Rd

step_sec_detector_delay() creates a specification of a recipe step that aligns detector signals to a reference detector in multi-detector SEC systems.

Usage

step_sec_detector_delay(
  recipe,
  reference = NULL,
  targets = NULL,
  delay_volumes = NULL,
  delay_times = NULL,
  flow_rate = 1,
  method = c("shift", "interpolate"),
  role = NA,
  trained = FALSE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("sec_detector_delay"),
  elution_units = "min"
)

Arguments

recipe

A recipe object.

reference

Character name of the reference detector column. The reference is unchanged and cannot also be a target.

targets

Character vector of detector columns to shift. If NULL, all measure columns except the reference are shifted. character() selects no target columns.

delay_volumes

Named numeric vector of delay volumes in mL. Names must identify target columns. Positive values indicate that the target detector sees the sample after the reference.

delay_times

Named numeric vector of delay times in minutes. This is an alternative to delay_volumes; the values remain in minutes in the step object.

flow_rate

Flow rate in mL/min. Required only when converting between time and volume axes. Any supplied value must be positive and finite.

method

Method for shifting signals: "shift" (index shift with round-to-even quantization) or "interpolate" (piecewise-linear interpolation).

role

Not used by this step.

trained

Logical indicating if the step has been trained.

skip

Logical. Should the step be skipped when baking?

id

Unique step identifier.

elution_units

Units of the measure location coordinates: "min" (minutes), "s" (seconds), "mL" (millilitres), or "uL" (microlitres). The default is "min".

Value

An updated recipe with the new step added.

Details

Detector delay declarations retain their own dimensions: delay_times are always minutes and delay_volumes are always millilitres, regardless of elution_units. The step converts the declared delay to the location axis units during baking. Time-to-time and volume-to-volume conversions do not need a flow rate. Converting between time and volume needs a positive finite flow_rate in mL/min.

A corrected target value at location x is evaluated at x + delay. Thus, a positive delay moves target values toward lower locations. The reference and every target curve in a current bake row must have exactly the same numeric location grid. This step does not resample mismatched grids.

The "shift" method requires a nonzero-delay grid to be uniformly spaced; adjacent widths may differ by at most 1e-8 relative to the first width. Delays are rounded to the nearest whole index using R's round-to-even rule. A zero delay is an exact pass-through and does not require uniform spacing. The "interpolate" method accepts irregular monotonic grids, returns NA outside the sampled range, and propagates missing values without bridging an internal NA gap. Neither method changes the location coordinates.

elution_units is a caller declaration. This step does not infer units from record metadata or add an axis-unit attribute to measure columns.

See also

Other sec-chromatography: step_sec_band_broadening(), step_sec_baseline(), step_sec_exclude_regions(), step_sec_integration_window(), step_sec_mw_averages(), step_sec_mw_distribution(), step_sec_mw_fractions(), step_sec_peaks_deconvolve(), step_sec_peaks_detect(), step_sec_peaks_refine()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(recipes)
library(measure)

# Correct UV and MALS signals relative to RI on a minute axis
rec <- recipe(~., data = sec_triple_detect) |>
  step_measure_input_long(ri_signal, location = vars(elution_time), col_name = "ri") |>
  step_measure_input_long(uv_signal, location = vars(elution_time), col_name = "uv") |>
  step_measure_input_long(mals_signal, location = vars(elution_time), col_name = "mals") |>
  step_sec_detector_delay(
    reference = "ri",
    delay_volumes = c(uv = -0.05, mals = 0.15),
    elution_units = "min"
  ) |>
  prep()
} # }
